reasons: Error handling is tested only for the permanent 422 failure from OCR.
One test title says it checks document type normalization, but no check in that test looks at the document type.
Results depend on fake services, not real ones.

terms.meaning: a job queue that runs tasks in the background, outside the request that created them.
a fake stand-in for a real service, used so a test can run alone.
reading text from an image or scanned page.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for processor tests
sections.what: Loads the testing tools, the processor under test, and the stand-ins for storage, notifications and the database.

sections.name: DocumentProcessor (BullMQ OCR & AI Summarization Pipeline) (part 1)
sections.title: Fake services and processor setup
sections.what: Before each test, sets up fake database records, a fake file store that returns small test bytes, a fake web client, a fake notification sender and a fake config reader, then builds the processor with them.
sections.why: Likely reason: each test starts from the same clean state so one test cannot affect another.
sections.watch_out: Any new database call the processor makes must also be added to these fakes, or the test fails because the fake does not provide it.

sections.name: DocumentProcessor (BullMQ OCR & AI Summarization Pipeline) (part 2)
sections.title: Test setup for a normal lab report
sections.what: Starts the normal lab report test by defining a fake job and a fake successful OCR reply containing one glucose reading.
sections.why: Likely reason: a realistic reply lets the test follow the normal path through the processor.

sections.name: DocumentProcessor (BullMQ OCR & AI Summarization Pipeline) (part 3)
sections.title: Successful AI summary and embedding replies
sections.what: Defines fake successful AI summary and embedding replies with no risk flags, routes each web call to its fake reply, runs the processor, and checks that the virus scan marked the file clean.
sections.why: Likely reason: the test covers each stage of the pipeline in order.

sections.name: DocumentProcessor (BullMQ OCR & AI Summarization Pipeline) (part 4)
sections.title: Normal report checks and critical setup
sections.what: Checks that the AI summary is marked complete and that a normal report sends an info notice titled Medical Report Analyzed. Then starts the critical test with a fake job and fake glucose and HbA1c readings.
sections.why: Likely reason: confirming the normal case stays at info level makes the critical escalation test meaningful.
sections.watch_out: The happy path test title mentions document type normalization, yet no assertion in that test checks the document type.

sections.name: DocumentProcessor (BullMQ OCR & AI Summarization Pipeline) (part 5)
sections.title: Critical findings and failed read setup
sections.what: Sets up the critical case so the AI reply lists two critical risk flags, then sets up a failure case with a new fake job for a corrupted scan.
sections.why: Likely reason: high readings test the escalation rule with realistic critical values.

sections.name: DocumentProcessor (BullMQ OCR & AI Summarization Pipeline) (part 6)
sections.title: OCR rejection and withdrawn consent tests
sections.what: Makes the OCR service reply with a 422 error, then checks that the OCR status is marked FAILED and the user gets an alert asking for a re-upload. Starts the withdrawn consent test by simulating a withdrawn AI consent and checking that no AI call is made.
sections.why: Likely reason: a 422 means the file itself cannot be read, so the user must upload it again, and the test checks that path.
sections.watch_out: The alert check matches the word re-upload in the message body, so rewording that message breaks the test.

sections.name: DocumentProcessor (BullMQ OCR & AI Summarization Pipeline) (part 7)
sections.title: Withheld status check and test group end
sections.what: Checks that the AI summary is marked withheld, which holds the document until the user grants consent. Closes the test groups.
sections.why: Likely reason: withheld is a separate state, so processing can resume once consent is given.
sections.watch_out: Nothing in this test covers what happens after consent is granted, which is handled by the separate reprocess action.

summary: Automated tests for the background job that scans, reads and summarizes uploaded medical documents, covering success, critical findings, a failed read, and missing consent.
purpose: Confirms the processor moves a document through its steps, sets the right statuses, and sends the right alerts, using fake versions of the database, storage, AI service and notifications.
why: Likely reason: medical processing has many branches, so tests protect the important ones, such as raising critical findings and blocking AI use without consent.
how: 1) Build fake database, storage, web client, notification and config objects. 2) Create the processor using those fakes. 3) Run each scenario with a fake job. 4) Check the statuses written, the alerts sent, and whether the AI service was called.
inputs: Fake job data with document id, user id, file key, file type and the list of steps to run, plus fake replies from the OCR and AI services.
outputs: Pass or fail results from the test runner. No real files or services are used.
risks: Because everything is faked, the tests cannot show that the real OCR or AI services reply the way the fakes do. The fake web client finds each service by matching part of the web address, so changing those addresses makes the fakes return empty data and the tests fail in confusing ways.
debug: If a test fails, read the expected and received values in the output, then check the fake reply for that scenario. If OCR tests fail after a code change, confirm the web address paths in the processor still contain the same parts.
